experiment: Paired tail-rate ratio on hard328: the pooled rate of sampled tokens with p < 0.01 per generated token, RL plain over base cue, on problems both models finished. This tests the mechanism against tail trimming: the rival r3-surprises-1 (RL trims the tail everywhere) predicts about 0.6 or less, and this mechanism predicts about 1.
recipe: Files: S3 r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue) and r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151540-86ef/answers.jsonl (RL plain), fetched with the aws commands in inventory.md. In each file keep one row per problem_index: the one with the smallest attempt, or the first in file order if there is no attempt field. Keep the problem_index values present in both files whose kept rows have cap_hit false in both files. Drop a problem from both models if either row has a null or missing n_tok_p_lt_1e2 or n_generated, or n_generated == 0. For each model, rate = sum of n_tok_p_lt_1e2 / sum of n_generated over the kept problems, pooled, not a mean of per-row rates. Statistic = rate(86ef) / rate(e72c). No grading is used.

experiment: Cause: whether the cued base's wrong answers carry more low-probability tokens than its right ones at matched length, on hard328. This mechanism (errors are drawn from the head) predicts a ratio near 1. A tail-derailment account (unlikely tokens push answers off course) predicts about 1.3 or more.
recipe: File: S3 r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue). Keep one row per problem_index (smallest attempt, else first in file order). Keep rows with cap_hit false, non-null n_tok_p_lt_1e2 and n_generated > 0. Right = score_v3 == 1, and wrong = any other value, with null counting as wrong. Sort the kept rows by n_generated ascending, ties broken by problem_index ascending. Give each row its 0-based rank r and quartile q = floor(4*r/N), where N is the number of kept rows. In each quartile compute rW = sum n_tok_p_lt_1e2 / sum n_generated over the wrong rows and rR the same over the right rows. Skip a quartile with no wrong rows, no right rows, or rR == 0. ratio_q = rW / rR. Statistic = sum over kept quartiles of (number of wrong rows in q) * ratio_q / sum over kept quartiles of (number of wrong rows in q).
unit: ratio of pooled rates (wrong / right), wrong-count-weighted over length quartiles

experiment: Where the effect should not appear: on hard328 problems where the cued base finished wrong and RL finished, whether RL's tail-rate change relative to the base differs between problems RL fixes and problems it does not. The tail-trimming rival puts the fix where the tail was cut, a clearly negative difference of about -0.3. This mechanism (fixes come from head swaps) predicts about 0.
recipe: Files: e72c (base cue) and 86ef (RL plain) answers.jsonl as in the first prediction, one row per problem_index each (smallest attempt, else first in file order). Keep problems present in both files where the e72c row has cap_hit false and score_v3 != 1 (null counts as not 1), and the 86ef row has cap_hit false. Drop a problem if either row has a null or missing n_tok_p_lt_1e2 or n_generated, or n_generated == 0. Per problem d = ln((t_RL + 0.5) / g_RL) - ln((t_b + 0.5) / g_b), with t = n_tok_p_lt_1e2 and g = n_generated of that model's row. Fixed = 86ef score_v3 == 1, and unfixed = otherwise. Statistic = (mean d over fixed problems) - (mean d over unfixed problems). If either group is empty, the statistic counts as refuted.
unit: difference of mean natural-log rate ratios

experiment: Mechanism test: ratio of the self-inconsistent-equation rate of the cued base at T 1.0 to the same rate at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, on problems where both answers finished. This mechanism (tail draws at result tokens) predicts about 3. The systematic-error rival (result-faf15a's 'not an unlikely sample' reading) predicts about 1.0 (0.8 to 1.3).
recipe:
Files: A = runs/theory-rows/s3new/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl; base, cue, T 1.0) and B = runs/theory-rows/s3new/r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl; base, cue, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95), plus studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json (field subject). In A keep the first row per problem_index in file order. In B keep, per problem_index, the row with the smallest sample value (first in file order on ties). S = problem_index values with a kept row in both files, cap_hit false in both, and per_problem.json subject != 'Number Theory'. EQ procedure, per row: (1) t = text with re.sub(r'(?<=\d),(?=\d{3})', '', text). (2) For each m in re.finditer(r'(?<![\d.])(\d{1,3})\s*(\+|-|\*|×|\times|\cdot)\s*(\d{1,3})\s*=\s*(\d{1,6})(?!\d)', t): (3) pre_s = t[:m.start()].rstrip(' 	'); keep only if pre_s == '' or pre_s[-1] in '
$=:,(' or re.search(r'(?:^|[\s(])[A-Za-z]{2,}$', pre_s). (4) post = t[m.end():]; post_s = post.lstrip(' 	'); drop if re.match(r'[A-Za-z^_/({]', post) or re.match(r'\.\d', post) or re.match(r'[+\-*/^×]|\(times|cdot|div|frac|sqrt|pmod|bmod|mod)|\(\s*\?mod|mod ', post_s). (5) Drop if the line holding m.start() (from the previous '
' to the next '
') contains '?'. (6) a, b, c = int of groups 1, 3, 4; op = add for '+', sub for '-', mul for the others; drop sub with a < b. (7) The equation is wrong iff the op applied to a, b != c. (8) Per row, deduplicate by the tuple (a, op, b, c): N_row = number of distinct tuples, W_row = number of distinct wrong tuples. Sum over the S rows of each file: N_A, W_A, N_B, W_B. Statistic R = ((W_A + 0.5) / N_A) / ((W_B + 0.5) / N_B). If N_A or N_B is 0, the prediction counts as refuted. Cap hits are excluded through S, and missing rows exclude the problem.

experiment: Cause (RL sharpened the result positions): ratio of RL's self-inconsistent-equation rate at T 1.0 to the cued base's at T 1.0, on problems where both finished.
recipe: Files: A = runs/theory-rows/s3new/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (base, cue, T 1.0) and C = runs/theory-rows/s3new/r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl; RL, plain, T 1.0), plus studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json (subject). experiment: Effect in accuracy: paired finished-answer error, plain T 1.0 minus the entropy-gated arm that samples at T 0.6 where entropy <= 0.9 nats (confident positions, which include result tokens), on (problem, sample) pairs where both finished.
recipe: Files: E = studies/rlneurons/results/egate/math500_lo6-01/rows.jsonl (4 samples per problem) and D = studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl. For each (problem_index, sample) in E, take the first E row in file order and the first D row in file order with the same problem_index, attempt == 0 and the same sample. Drop the pair if either row is missing. A row is a cap hit if cap_hit is true, or if cap_hit is missing and finish_reason == 'length'. Keep pairs where neither row is a cap hit. wrong = 1 unless score_v3 == 1 (null or missing counts as wrong). Statistic = mean wrong over the kept D rows minus mean wrong over the kept E rows.

experiment: Where the effect should not appear: the same paired finished-answer error difference for the arm that samples at T 0.6 only where entropy > 0.9 nats (forks). Result tokens are low-entropy positions, so this mechanism predicts no gain. A fork-centred reading (2506.01939) would expect forks to matter most.
recipe: Files: H = studies/rlneurons/results/egate/math500_hi6-01/rows.jsonl (2 samples per problem) and D = studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl. Pair, filter and score exactly as in the previous recipe, with H in place of E: for each (problem_index, sample) in H, the first H row and the first D row with attempt == 0 and the same sample; drop missing pairs; cap hit = cap_hit true, or cap_hit missing and finish_reason == 'length'; keep pairs with no cap hit on either side; wrong = 1 unless score_v3 == 1. Statistic = mean wrong over the kept D rows minus mean wrong over the kept H rows.

experiment: Mechanism test, problem dependence of misread and slip steps. Among the wrongstep items labelled misread or slip, the fraction with g > 0, where g = (lp_span - lp_control) under the base scored with the problem text deleted ('noprob') minus the same under the plain base. This mechanism predicts well above half (deleting the problem removes evidence against the step, but not the step's own support). The uniform-hazard rival predicts about 0.5. The problem-induced-misread rival (m04) predicts below 0.5.
recipe: File: studies/rlneurons/results/wrongstep/rules-01/items.json (51 rows). For each row read models['base'] and models['noprob'], fields lp_span and lp_control, as stored, with no rescaling. Keep rows whose label, lowercased, contains the substring 'misread' or the substring 'slip'. Drop a row if either model entry, or any of the four numbers, is missing or null. X_m = lp_span(m) - lp_control(m). g = X_noprob - X_base. A row counts if g > 0 strictly; g == 0 counts as not positive. Statistic = counted rows / kept rows. If fewer than 10 rows are kept, the prediction counts as refuted.

experiment: Cause test, mode vs tail. On all 51 wrongstep items, the fraction whose wrong step gains on control text when the base is rescored at T 0.6: (lp_span - lp_control) under 't0.6' minus the same under 'base', counted when positive. This mechanism (the step sits near the mode) predicts more than half. The tail-token rival (r3-surprises-1: errors are low-probability draws) predicts below half, because a cooler distribution penalises the step more than ordinary text.
recipe: File: studies/rlneurons/results/wrongstep/rules-01/items.json. For each row read models['base'] and models['t0.6'], fields lp_span and lp_control, as stored. Use all labels. Drop a row if either model entry or any of the four numbers is missing or null. X_m = lp_span(m) - lp_control(m). d = X_t0.6 - X_base. A row counts if d > 0 strictly; ties count as not positive. Statistic = counted rows / kept rows. If fewer than 20 rows are kept, the prediction counts as refuted.

experiment: Case where the effect should not appear: wrong-plan items. The fraction of wrongstep items labelled as a wrong plan with g > 0 (g defined as in the first prediction: noprob minus base, each lp_span - lp_control). This mechanism says a plan is chosen in response to the problem, so deleting the problem should not favour it the way it favours misreads and slips. It predicts a share near or below half, well under the misread/slip share. A reader who takes g > 0 as a generic effect of shorter context predicts the same share as the misread/slip items.
recipe: File: studies/rlneurons/results/wrongstep/rules-01/items.json. Keep rows whose label, lowercased, contains the substring 'plan' and contains neither 'misread' nor 'slip'. Read models['base'] and models['noprob'], fields lp_span and lp_control, as stored. Drop a row if any of the four numbers or either model entry is missing or null. g = (lp_span - lp_control)_noprob - (lp_span - lp_control)_base. Count rows with g > 0 strictly (ties not positive). Statistic = counted / kept. If fewer than 6 rows are kept, the prediction counts as refuted.

experiment: Phenomenon on Math: Math 3.1 cue minus Math 3.0 cue right answers in the longest quartile of MATH-500 by RL (T2) answer length, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, one sample each.
recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/axis/math500-01/vectors.json (with its manifest.json) and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. Arms: M30 = the arm whose manifest model is allenai/Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Math with the cue prompt; M31 = the arm named rl_cue if present, otherwise the first arm in manifest order whose manifest model is allenai/Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math with the cue prompt and no weight edit. Align each arm's 0/1 v3 vector to problem_index through vectors.json problem_indices. Quartiles: sort the 500 problems by t2_generated_tokens ascending, ties broken by problem_index ascending; Q4 = ranks 376-500 (cap hits at their stored token count). A problem missing from an arm counts 0 in that arm; cap hits are whatever 0/1 the vector holds. Statistic: (sum of M31 over Q4) minus (sum of M30 over Q4), a signed integer.

experiment: Where the effect should not appear: Math 3.1 cue minus Math 3.0 cue right answers on the shorter half (Q1+Q2 by T2 length) of MATH-500, T 1.0. A stop-early policy loses nothing on short problems; a uniform-deficit rival spreads the 9-problem overall gap (457 vs 448) over all lengths, about +4 to +5 here.
recipe: Same files, arms, alignment and missing-row rule as the previous prediction. Q1+Q2 = the 250 problems with the lowest t2_generated_tokens (ties by problem_index ascending; ranks 1-250). Statistic: (sum of M31 over Q1+Q2) minus (sum of M30 over Q1+Q2), a signed integer.

experiment: Mechanism test (length shortening confined to long problems), Math 3.0 first release vs Math 3.1 step 2,800, plain MATH-500, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95: median log ratio of finished lengths in the top T2-length quartile minus the same in the short half. The nearest rival (3.0 is a uniformly less-trained policy, shorter by the same factor everywhere) predicts about 0.00; this mechanism predicts clearly negative.
recipe: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/fr-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (A, first release = 3.0) and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s2800-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (B, 3.1 step 2,800), fetched as in inventory.md, and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. Quartiles from per_problem.json: sort the 500 problems by t2_generated_tokens ascending, ties by problem_index ascending; Q4 = ranks 376-500, short half = ranks 1-250. experiment: Cause test, the 12k cliff: among finished MATH-500 answers at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 (plain and cue pooled), the ratio of answers of at least 12,000 tokens to answers of 8,000-11,999 tokens, Math 3.0 first release divided by Math 3.1 step 2,800. A uniform-shortening rival gives about 0.8 to 1.0; a 12k training budget gives a clear cliff.
recipe: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/fr-01/out/P_math500.jsonl and .../fr-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (3.0), s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s2800-01/out/P_math500.jsonl and .../s2800-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (3.1), fetched as in inventory.md. Pool each model's P and F kept rows. For each model, A_m = number of pooled rows with 8000 <= n_new < 12000 and B_m = number with n_new >= 12000. R_m = B_m / A_m. Statistic = R(3.0) / R(3.1). experiment: Mechanism test, concentration of Code 3.1's wrong-step lowering on Math 3.1's strongest-veto items: the share of the summed Code 3.1 D that falls on the third of items where Math 3.1's D is most negative. The uniform-partial-copy rival (Code 3.1's lowering spread over items independently of Math's) predicts about 0.33, and at most about 0.45 with shared item effects. The veto mechanism predicts most of the sum.
recipe: File: studies/rlneurons/results/wrongstep/math500-01/items.json (a list of 51 item objects). For each item and model name m in {base, code31, math31}, read models[m].lp_span and models[m].lp_control. D_m = (lp_span_m - lp_control_m) - (lp_span_base - lp_control_base). Drop any item where any of these six numbers is missing or null. Sort the kept items by D_math31 ascending, ties broken by problem_index ascending, then by sample ascending. T = the first floor(n/3) items of that order, where n = number of kept items. Statistic C = (sum of D_code31 over T) / (sum of D_code31 over all kept items). If the denominator is >= 0, C is undefined and counts as refuted.

experiment: Where a veto cannot create a path: Code 3.1 cue single-sample accuracy on the MATH-500 problems where the cued base is right in none of its 4 stored samples. A veto removes the base's sampled wrong steps but installs no new solution route, so Code 3.1 should stay near a fresh base sample there and well below RL's own rate.

Use arms 'base_cue_s0', 'base_cue_s1', 'base_cue_s2', 'base_cue_s3' and 'code_cue' (Code-RL 3.1, cue), each a v3 0/1 vector aligned to problem_indices (cap hits are already 0). experiment: Mechanism test, recurrence across prompts. On problems the cued base solves 4 of 4, take the problems where Think-SFT with the cue gives a finished wrong answer, and compute the fraction where Think-SFT plain is also wrong. A deterministic format miss recurs. The independent-slip rival predicts about Think-SFT plain's error rate on these easy problems, about 0.05 (at most about 0.2 with difficulty correlation).
recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl, studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/sft1_cue-01/per_problem.json, studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/sft1_plain-01/per_problem.json. E4 = problem_index values with exactly 4 rows in rows.jsonl having attempt == 0, all 4 with score_v3 == 1 and cap_hit not true. In each per_problem.json keep the first row per problem_index in file order. W = E4 problems whose sft1_cue row has score_v3 == 0 and cap_hit not true (rows with null or missing score_v3 that are not cap hits are excluded). For each problem in W, take its sft1_plain row; drop the problem if there is no row, or if the row has a null or missing score_v3 and is not a cap hit. Plain wrong = score_v3 == 0 or cap_hit true. Statistic = (problems in W with plain wrong) / (problems in W kept). If no problem is kept, the prediction counts as refuted.

experiment: Cause, answer-type dependence. Among the problems in W (cued base 4 of 4, Think-SFT cue finished wrong), the share whose gold is not a plain integer. Format misses fall on non-integer answer types (fractions, expressions, tuples, text, units). The reasoning-slip rival predicts the share of non-integer golds in the whole 4-of-4 pool, about 0.35 to 0.4.
recipe: Files and the sets E4 and W exactly as in the recurrence recipe. Gold of a problem = the gold field of its first attempt-0 row in rows.jsonl (file order). Normalise: strip outer whitespace, remove every '$' and all whitespace, and if the result is wholly \boxed{...} take the inside. Then delete commas that sit between a digit and exactly three digits (regex (?<=\d),(?=\d{3}(?!\d)) replaced by ''). The gold is an integer iff the result fully matches ^-?\d+$. Statistic = (problems in W whose gold is not an integer) / (problems in W). If W is empty, the prediction counts as refuted.

experiment: A case where Think-SFT's dominant failure should not appear: the share of cap hits among Think-SFT cue's wrong answers on problems the cued base solves 4 of 4. Over all 500 problems, cap hits make up 0.52 of Think-SFT's wrong answers (facts.json). An overthinking rival, in which easy problems also fail by running long, predicts about that share here. This mechanism says the easy-side errors are finished answers.
recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl and studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/sft1_cue-01/per_problem.json. E4 as in the recurrence recipe. In sft1_cue keep the first row per problem_index in file order. Wrong = score_v3 == 0 or cap_hit true; rows with null or missing score_v3 that are not cap hits are excluded. Among E4 problems whose sft1_cue row is wrong, statistic = (rows with cap_hit true) / (wrong rows). If there are no wrong rows, the prediction counts as refuted.

experiment: Mechanism test, normal length. On problems the cued base solves 4 of 4, compare Think-SFT cue's finished-wrong and finished-right answers by their length relative to RL's length on the same problem, as a difference of medians of a log ratio. A rejected but complete solution is as long as a right one, about 0. The reasoning-failure rival predicts clearly longer wrong answers: about +0.2 for the base's own wrong siblings (facts.json, r5-m02), and +0.8 or more for long-CoT models (2501.18585).
recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl, studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/sft1_cue-01/per_problem.json, studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. E4 as in the recurrence recipe. In each per_problem.json keep the first row per problem_index in file order. Keep E4 problems whose sft1_cue row has cap_hit not true and a non-null score_v3, and whose t1_t2_items row has a non-null t2_generated_tokens. For each kept problem x = ln(max(n_generated, 1) / max(t2_generated_tokens, 1)), with n_generated from sft1_cue. experiment: Mechanism test: within-cue wrong-answer agreement minus cue-vs-plain wrong-answer agreement on MATH-500 at T 1.0, A - B. The problem-driven-attractor rival predicts about 0.00 (a problem's common wrong value is hit by any base context); this mechanism predicts clearly positive.
recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (CUE) and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl (T3, plain base, T 1.0; fetch with the aws command in inventory.md). CUE: keep rows with attempt == 0; for each (problem_index, sample) keep the first row in file order. A CUE row is a wrong answer iff cap_hit is not true, finish_reason != 'length', score_v3 == 0, and extracted_v3 is a non-empty string after strip(). T3: keep the first row per problem_index in file order; run grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py, the procedure that fills score_v3 and extracted_v3) on its text and gold to get its v3 score and v3 extracted answer. A T3 row is a wrong answer iff cap_hit is not true, finish_reason != 'length', v3 score == 0 and the v3 extracted answer is non-empty after strip(). Agreement of two answers = rln4_lib.agree(a, b) from studies/rlneurons/lib/rln4_lib.py (true = agree). A = (number of unordered pairs of CUE wrong answers of the same problem_index that agree) / (number of such pairs), pooled over problems. B = (number of (CUE wrong answer, T3 wrong answer) pairs with the same problem_index that agree) / (number of such pairs), pooled over problems. Statistic = A - B. Problems with fewer than two CUE wrong answers contribute no A pairs; problems without a T3 wrong answer contribute no B pairs. If either denominator is 0 the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.

experiment: Case where the effect should not appear: changing only the sampling rule under the same cue (T 1.0 / min-p 0.1) should keep the wrong values. Cross-file agreement C between day1_3 cued wrong answers and min-p cued wrong answers, minus within-file agreement A. A sampling-driven account (wrong values are per-draw accidents that any change of the sampler reshuffles) predicts C well below A.
recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (CUE) and iterate-runs:frustea-1114-180849-456c/answers.jsonl (MINP, base, cue, T 1.0 / min-p 0.1; local copy runs/theory-rows/frustea-1114-180849-456c/answers.jsonl per inventory.md). CUE rows, CUE wrong answers, agreement (rln4_lib.agree from studies/rlneurons/lib/rln4_lib.py) and A exactly as in the first prediction (attempt == 0, first row per (problem_index, sample); wrong answer = cap_hit not true, finish_reason != 'length', score_v3 == 0, non-empty stripped extracted_v3; A = agreeing unordered same-problem pairs / all such pairs, pooled). MINP: keep rows with attempt == 0 or no attempt field, then the first row per problem_index in file order; a MINP row is a wrong answer under the same rule using its stored score_v3 and extracted_v3. C = (number of (CUE wrong answer, MINP wrong answer) pairs with the same problem_index that agree) / (number of such pairs), pooled. Statistic = C - A. If either denominator is 0 the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.

experiment: Cause of the vote shortfall: among MATH-500 problems where the cued base has at least one right sample of 4 but the plurality vote is wrong, the share where the winning answer group has two or more members (agreeing wrong values), against singleton ties.
recipe: File: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl. Keep rows with attempt == 0 and, for each (problem_index, sample) with sample in {0,1,2,3}, the first row in file order; keep problems that have all 4 samples. A sample is answer-bearing iff cap_hit is not true, finish_reason != 'length' and extracted_v3 is non-empty after strip(). A sample is right iff it is answer-bearing and score_v3 == 1. Grouping: process answer-bearing samples in increasing sample index; each joins the first existing group whose first member agrees with it under rln4_lib.agree (studies/rlneurons/lib/rln4_lib.py), else starts a new group. Winner = the group with the most members; ties go to the group whose first member has the lowest sample index. The vote is right iff the winner's first member has score_v3 == 1; with no answer-bearing sample the vote is wrong. F = problems with at least one right sample whose vote is wrong. Statistic = (problems in F whose winning group has 2 or more members) / |F|. If F is empty the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.

experiment: Mechanism test: per-problem gain of the RL-written-examples arm (draw 1) over the mean of the 4 cued-base samples, averaged over problems in the subjects of example problems 0-2, minus the same average over all other subjects. The register-transfer rival (gain spread in proportion to base errors) predicts about 0.015; subject confinement predicts about 0.08.
recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/axis/math500-01/vectors.json with its manifest.json, and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. Arm R = the vectors.json arm whose manifest entry is the cued base with 3 solved examples written by Math-RL (Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math) of MATH-500 problems 0, 1, 2 (shots1, draw 1). Arms B0-B3 = base_cue_s0, base_cue_s1, base_cue_s2, base_cue_s3. Align every arm to problem_index through vectors.json problem_indices. Drop problem_index 0, 1 and 2, and any problem whose entry in R or in any B arm is null or missing. Per problem b = (B0+B1+B2+B3)/4 and g = R - b; vector entries are v3 0/1, and cap hits are already 0. M = the set of per_problem.json subject values of problem_index 0, 1 and 2. Statistic S = mean of g over the kept problems whose per_problem.json subject is in M, minus mean of g over the kept problems whose subject is not in M. Problems absent from per_problem.json are dropped.

experiment: Case where the effect should not appear: the same matched-minus-unmatched contrast for the base-written-examples arm, which uses the same three example problems and so the same subjects. The examples carry the base's own routine, so the mechanism predicts no subject contrast.
recipe: Files as in the first recipe. Arm E = the vectors.json arm whose manifest job id is abaybektursun-1114-183855-e840 (cued base with 3 base-written examples). Arms B0-B3 = base_cue_s0 to base_cue_s3. Drop problem_index 0, 1, 2 and any problem whose entry in E or in any B arm is null or missing. Per problem g = E - (B0+B1+B2+B3)/4. M = subjects of problem_index 0, 1, 2 in per_problem.json. Statistic S_E = mean g over kept problems with subject in M minus mean g over kept problems with subject not in M. Problems absent from per_problem.json are dropped.

experiment: Cause: the examples only let the base copy a routine on problems it can already solve. On problems the cued base solved in 0 of its 4 samples, the RL-written-examples arm should do no better than a fresh base sample (about 5 right). A rival in which the examples pass on RL's capability predicts about RL's single-sample rate there, about 9 to 10.
recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/axis/math500-01/vectors.json with manifest.json. Arm R as in the first recipe (Math-RL-written examples of problems 0-2, draw 1); B0-B3 = base_cue_s0 to base_cue_s3. Drop problem_index 0, 1, 2 and any problem whose entry in R or in any B arm is null or missing. Z = kept problems with B0+B1+B2+B3 == 0. Statistic = number of problems in Z where R == 1 (an integer; cap hits are already 0 in the vectors). Also report |Z|.
